data.title: Mink Ventures Closes $521,298 In First Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mink Ventures Corporation (“Mink” or the "Company") announces it has closed the first tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the “Offering”) announced on October 29, 2026. The Company has raised gross proceeds of $521,298 from the issuance of 1,188,100 hard dollar units (the "HD Units") at a price of $0.08 per HD Unit and the issuance of 4,059,524 CMETC eligible flow-through units (the “FT Units”) at a price of $0.105 per FT Unit in this first tranche. A second and final closing of the Offering is expected to occur on December 2, 2026.

Each HD Unit consists of one common share of the Company (a “Common Share”) and one Common Share purchase warrant (“HD Warrant”). Each HD Warrant shall entitle the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16.

Each FT Unit consists of one Common Share of the Company (a “FT Share”) and one Common Share purchase warrant (“FT Warrant”). Each FT Warrant shall entitle the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16.

The FT Shares were issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the “Tax Act”). An amount equal to the portion of the subscription price that is directly attributable to the consideration paid for the subscription and issuance of the FT Shares will be used to incur eligible resource exploration expenses which will qualify as (i) “Canadian exploration expenses” (as defined in the Tax Act), and (ii) “flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures” (as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Tax Act) (collectively, the “Qualifying Expenditures”). Qualifying Expenditures in an aggregate amount equal to the gross proceeds raised from the issuance of the FT Shares will be renounced to the initial purchasers of the FT Units with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The FT Warrants were not issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of the Tax Act.

All securities issued in the closing of this tranche of the Offering are subject to statutory four month plus a day hold periods expiring on March 20, 2027. The Offering is subject to obtaining final approval of the TSX Venture Exchange.

Certain directors and officers of the Company purchased an aggregate of 63,100 HD Units pursuant to the Offering, constituting a “related party transaction” as such term is defined by Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”). The transaction will be exempt from the MI 61-101 valuation and minority approval requirements for related party transactions in connection with the Offering under sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 as neither the fair market value (as determined under MI 61-101) of the subject matter of, nor the fair market value of the consideration for, the transaction, insofar as it involves the related party, exceeds 25% of the Company’s market capitalization (as determined under MI 61-101).

The Company paid aggregate cash finder’s fees totaling $40,020 and issued 398,761 in non-transferable finder's warrants (the "Finder's Warrants"). Each Finder's Warrant entitles the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16. All of the finder’s fees are subject to compliance with applicable securities legislation and TSX Venture Exchange policies.

The Company plans to use the net proceeds raised from the sale of the FT Units under the Offering for the exploration and advancement of the Company’s, Timmins area, critical minerals projects covering 115 km2, which include the Montcalm Ni Cu Co project, the Warren Cu Ni Co project, and the Rankin Cu Ni Co project; and, in respect of the HD Unit proceeds under the Offering, for general working capital purposes.

About Mink Ventures Corporation:

Mink Ventures Corporation is a Canadian mineral exploration company exploring for critical minerals in Ontario, Canada. It has a prospective, nickel copper cobalt exploration portfolio, with its Montcalm project, which now covers approximately 104 km2 adjacent to Glencore’s former Montcalm Mine with historical production of 3.93 million tonnes of ore grading 1.25% Ni, 0.67% Cu and 0.051% Co (Ontario Geological Survey, Atkinson, 2010), as well as its 11 km2 Warren Ni Cu Co Project and its newly optioned Rankin Cu Ni Co Property. These complementary nickel copper cobalt projects have excellent access and infrastructure and are in close proximity to the Timmins Mining Camp. The Company has 46,919,920 common shares outstanding after giving affect to this tranche of the Offering.

For further information about Mink Ventures Corporation please contact: Natasha Dixon, President & CEO, T: 250-882-5620 E: ndixon@minkventures.com or Kevin Filo, Director, T: 705-266-6818 or visit www.minkventures.com or www.sedarplus.ca

This press release includes certain "forward-looking statements" under applicable Canadian securities legislation, including, but not limited to, statements with respect to the completion and timing of the second tranche of the Offering, receipt of final approval of the TSX Venture Exchange, the proposed use of proceeds, and the exploration potential of the Company's mineral properties. data.title: Dow drops below 50K for the first time in 5 months
data.description:
U.S. equities retreated sharply on Thursday afternoon, pushing the Dow Jones Industrial Average below 50,000 for the first time since mid-June and to its lowest level since May 5.

The blue-chip index fell roughly 2% on the session and now stands -10.3% below its all-time trading high of 54,744, reached back on August 5.

The decline leaves the Dow more than 5,000 points off that peak, reflecting a sustained pullback from the summer highs.

Moreover, the leg lower on the session was fueled by basically all the components within the Dow, with 29 of the 30 names in the red. The one green spot belonged to Chevron .

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Swings Higher
data.description:

An analyst said he wasn't entirely sure as to what drove up canola Thursday, but noted it's "up one day, down the next" movement this week. The analyst suggested canola could see losses on Friday.

Although gains in crude oil turned softer on Thursday, there was still enough spillover to boost some of the vegetable oils, including canola. Additional support came from upticks in Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed.

Declines in Chicago soybeans and soymeal, plus those in Malaysian palm oil limited the upside in the Canadian oilseed.

The Canadian dollar was relatively steady on Thursday afternoon, with the loonie at 69.76 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 69.80.

data.title: Meta to price Muse Charm gadget at $300, The Information reports
data.description:
Meta Platforms plans to price its pocket-sized AI device, Muse Charm, at $300 and offer buyers up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon , the Information reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

  • Verizon did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment, while a Meta spokesperson said "we're charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we'll have more to share soon"

  • The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference

  • Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform

  • Users can tap the gadget to access Muse directly, bypassing AI apps on their smartphones

  • The device features a roughly 2-inch (5-cm) screen that can be navigated with a thumb, with a customizable Muse character at its center

  • A built-in 5G modem allows access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though it cannot make call

  • Muse has gained traction among users as Meta expands its push to make its AI assistant a more widely used consumer service

  • The AI agent allows users to delegate tasks such as shopping, travel booking and form-filling to an AI agent

  • Meta is expected to launch Charm in time for the holiday shopping season in December, according to Zuckerberg's comments at the company's Connect event.

data.title: A CoreWeave co-founder just made an unconventional $30 million wager on its battered bonds
data.description:
By Christine Ji

While executives typically buy shares to signal confidence, CoreWeave co-founder Brian Venturo is turning to the bond market to calm AI jitters

CoreWeave's 9.75% senior unsecured notes have recently traded around 81 cents on the dollar.

As CoreWeave faces concerns about its debt load and financial profile, one of its co-founders is responding with an unusual move.

CoreWeave (CRWV) co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo shared in a LinkedIn post Wednesday that he had purchased $30 million in face value of the company's unsecured bonds, which he intends to hold until maturity on Oct. 1, 2031.

"I've never been more confident in CoreWeave," he wrote. The company shared his statement in a social-media post on X.

Venturo's recent move was initially well received by investors, with CoreWeave shares rising as much as 10.5% Thursday. They've since turned negative amid broader pressure on the technology sector, and they're down nearly 50% since the beginning of October.

The SEC mandates that executives must file a public Form 4 within two business days whenever they buy or sell company stock or convertible bonds that can turn into stock. But no such rule applies to regular, nonconvertible bonds, meaning that the market didn't have knowledge of Venturo's purchase until he posted about it.

Insider purchases like Venturo's can signal management confidence in a company, although purchases of stock are far more typical. Executives who believe their company is undervalued can receive much more upside by buying stock. High-profile past examples of executives holding debt have usually been more extreme cases of downside protection. Former Sears CEO Eddie Lampert extended over $2.6 billion in loans to the struggling retailer through his hedge fund ahead of its 2018 bankruptcy.

Some commentators on social media also pointed out that Venturo had recently sold shares of CoreWeave. According to an SEC filing, he sold over 80,000 shares of the company in the three months ending Sept. 30.

CoreWeave didn't immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for comment.

Both CoreWeave's debt and equity have sold off due to artificial-intelligence jitters in recent months. The company's business model currently depends heavily on bringing data centers online with borrowed money, leaving it exposed to rising interest rates or slowdowns in demand for AI processing power. The bond series matching the maturity date that Venturo gave are CoreWeave's 9.75% senior unsecured notes, meaning that they aren't backed by company assets. These notes recently traded at roughly 81 cents on the dollar, according to LSEG.

CoreWeave had already taken steps to mitigate Wall Street's concerns, announcing during its recent third-quarter earnings call that it doesn't intend to tap the unsecured debt market for funding at current yields. Instead, the company said it will utilize customer prepayments and delay-draw term loans - facilities backed by specific customer contracts that allow it to borrow money in installments.

-Christine Ji

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: Fonterra lifts 2026-27 farmgate milk price forecast on China-led demand
data.description:
New Zealand dairy cooperative Fonterra raised its 2026-27 farmgate milk price forecast on Friday, aided by strong demand in China and elsewhere.

The company said it expects prices between NZ$9.60 and NZ$10.60 per kilogram of milk solids (kgMS), compared with its previous range of NZ$9 to NZ$10.50 per kgMS.

Here are the details:

  • The midpoint of the forecast now sits at NZ$10.10 per kgMS, compared with NZ$9.75 per kgMS earlier

  • "Whole and skim milk powder prices have continued to improve since our update last month, underpinned by strong Chinese buying and resilient demand across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa," CEO Richard Allen said

  • Fonterra said stronger milk powder prices were partly offset by weaker dairy fat prices

  • Although the company remains well hedged, it flagged foreign exchange volatility as a risk for the rest of the season

  • Fonterra said its organic milk price forecast range remains unchanged

data.title: Digi Power X adds 42 BTC, lifting its Bitcoin treasury to 259 BTC
data.description:
Digi Power X has raised its Bitcoin holdings by 42 BTC, bringing its total to 259 BTC.

That's a notable move for a company that has spent the past year or so trying to become an AI infrastructure business. The coins keep piling up even as the mining machines have mostly gone quiet.

Digi Power X, which trades on Nasdaq under the ticker DGXX, reported holding around 217 BTC as of June 30, 2026. At the time, that position was valued at approximately $12.7 million.

Bitcoin isn't the only digital asset on the books. As of that same June date, the company also held 1,017 ETH, worth roughly $1.6 million. Combined, its digital assets were valued at about $14.3 million.

What makes the latest jump interesting is the company's shrinking mining output. Digi Power X has been producing just 2-3 BTC per quarter recently, down from a previous range of 10-14 BTC.

Through the first nine months of 2026, the company mined only 5 BTC. Over the same stretch the year before, it mined 33.

At 2-3 BTC per quarter, accumulating 42 BTC through mining alone would take roughly 14 to 21 quarters. Whatever is filling the treasury, it isn't primarily the hash rate.

Digi Power X used to be called Digihost Technology Inc. and rebranded in March 2025.

The company has been moving away from pure crypto mining and toward AI-focused data center operations, including GPU rentals through its NeoCloudz platform.

The Q3 2026 earnings report showed how far that shift has progressed. Total revenue came in at $12.25 million, up 85% quarter-over-quarter and 50% year-over-year.

AI services accounted for 46% of that revenue.

The balance sheet is also in tidy shape. Digi Power X reported $119.6 million in cash and digital currencies and zero debt.

On the infrastructure side, the company is targeting more than 400 MW of energy generation capacity. It is also deploying modular Tier III facilities designed for high-density computing, the kind of setup AI customers tend to require.

Management has said it wants to keep a diversified revenue mix. That includes mining, colocation fees, and treasury management, which means it still holds onto the digital assets it accumulates rather than treating Bitcoin purely as inventory.

With $119.6 million in cash and digital currencies and no debt, the company has room to hold a crypto treasury without betting the business on it.

With 259 BTC on the books, Bitcoin price swings will show up more noticeably in the company's reported asset values, even as its operating revenue leans further toward AI.

Mining output fell from 33 BTC to 5 BTC year-over-year through nine months, while total revenue still grew 50% year-over-year in Q3. The machines making Bitcoin have taken a back seat, and the business grew anyway.

Going forward, a few things deserve attention. First, whether AI revenue keeps climbing past its 46% share of the total. Second, how quickly new energy capacity comes online. Third, whether the Bitcoin treasury keeps growing at this pace, and what the company says about its treasury strategy as it does.

data.title: Why Walmart is making a bigger bet on fast-food delivery
data.description:
By Bill Peters

The retail giant says around 90% of spending at fast-food chains occurs within a few miles from a Walmart

Walmart reported quarterly earnings on Thursday.

As Walmart expands its delivery service, it also wants to handle more of your takeout orders.

During its quarterly earnings call on Thursday, the big-box chain (WMT) said it was using its vast online-ordering infrastructure to deliver more meals from fast-food restaurants to customers' homes, alongside groceries and other items. Walmart executives said chains like Papa John's (PZZA) were already on board and consumer interest was strong.

"If you think about it from our standpoint, it helps us capture more meal occasions, which then drives traffic as well as increased frequency to our site and to our app," David Guggina, the CEO of Walmart U.S., said during the call, according to an AlphaSense transcript.

"About 90% of QSR spend happens within a few miles of a Walmart," he noted, referring to quick-service restaurants. "So in Q3, we leaned in. We've now expanded to over 2,700 restaurant locations. We added Dunkin' this past quarter, we expanded Subway and we announced our partnership with Papa John's."

Guggina added that those restaurant deliveries helped "keep our drivers engaged" and strengthened the retailer's last-mile network, or the final stretch of an item's journey before it arrives at a customer's doorstep. The company said it was rapidly scaling the service and thinking of other ways to expand its delivery capabilities.

Walmart in June began allowing customers in some areas to order items from Subway through the Walmart app or the retailer's website, either on its own or with an order for other items via Walmart Express. The sandwich chain is already the biggest in-store restaurant at Walmart, following a partnership that started in 2004.

"The future of retail is about bringing more of customers' everyday needs into a single, seamless experience," Tracy Poulliot, executive vice president of e-commerce and marketing at Walmart U.S., said in a press release in June.

Apps like Instacart (CART) already handle deliveries from retailers like Walmart and Costco Wholesale (COST). Doordash (DASH), which wants to combine with Instacart, delivers from restaurants as well as retailers. Over the years, the delivery-app industry has consolidated and platforms have increasingly offered similar services to compete.

Walmart's quarterly results on Thursday squeaked past Wall Street's estimates, and the company raised its full-year earnings and same-store sales outlook. During the earnings call, Walmart CEO John Furner said that e-commerce drove the company's sales gains during its third quarter, which ran through October. The company's third-quarter e-commerce sales rose 17%.

Shares of Walmart were down 1.3% on Thursday. However, the stock was up 12.8% so far this year. Shares were trading at nearly $126, off highs of more than $130 reached earlier this year.

Furner on Thursday described Walmart's customers as "stable" and "resilient" as they navigate rising costs of living that have hit its lower-income shoppers harder. Analysts have said that Walmart's delivery ecosystem, and its efforts to make it faster, have helped it attract wealthier customers who have turned to the retailer in search of lower prices.

"We no longer see stores and e-commerce as separate, but connected parts of an integrated ecosystem," Furner said on Thursday's call. "We can now reach 96% of U.S. households in less than three hours, and 60% in less than 30 minutes."

-Bill Peters

data.title: Kalshi’s Quintenz says insider trading is ‘just easier to see’ in prediction markets than stocks
data.description:
Brian Quintenz, Kalshi board member and former commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, said there are far more insider trading cases in the stock market than in prediction markets, where it can be easier to see when someone has affected the outcome of an event they traded on.

"And there are by far more insider trading cases that happen in the stock market than anything that happens in the derivatives markets or in the prediction market space," Quintenz said Thursday at The Hill and The Block's Capitol Crypto Forum. "It's just easier to see because it's very direct."

Quintenz said the possibility of insider trading should not make a market illegal or invalid. He said enforcement after a violation should supplement the work exchanges do to prevent it, and added that there was more work to do.

“Capitol

Who should be allowed to trade?

Dan Berkovitz, vice chair of external and regulatory affairs at Millennium Management and a former CFTC commissioner, said federal and exchange rules already prohibit insider trading. He said exchanges also need rules on who can trade, including employees of organizations involved in a contract and people who can influence its outcome.

"So you need rules against insider trading, you need participation limits, and you need strict anti-manipulation provisions," Berkovitz said.

Berkovitz pointed to mention markets, where the outcome can depend on whether a person says a particular word or phrase. A person who can decide whether to say something can also decide the outcome of the contract, he said. Berkovitz welcomed the CFTC's guidance but said more work is needed on who has insider information or can influence the outcome.

"Who has influence or control of the contract? Who has insider knowledge? Those types of things, I think we can still use further development, but there's initial steps being taken to get there," Berkovitz said.

Christy Goldsmith Romero, senior fellow at the Atlantic Council and a former CFTC commissioner, said exchanges are the first line of defense against insider trading and that the CFTC probably needs to do more. She pointed to the requirement that exchanges certifying their own contracts attest that those contracts are not readily susceptible to manipulation. She added that greater clarity was needed from the CFTC to assist exchanges with that.

Quintenz agreed that more guidance would help. However, he said whether a contract is readily susceptible to manipulation is a judgment call and that the CFTC should explain how it applies the standard rather than leaving exchanges to come up with different standards on their own.

Regulation of sports contracts

The panel also discussed who should regulate sports event contracts. Berkovitz explained that the post-Dodd-Frank final rule continues to prohibit gaming contracts via the CFTC, subject only to future regulatory amendment. The latest interim rule, however, draws a distinction between gambling conducted at a casino and products listed for trading on a federally regulated exchange, Berkovitz said. He added that a legal question remains over whether essentially the same product can be treated as a swap on one platform but not another.

Quintenz said he had submitted a comment letter in his personal capacity, noting that the Supreme Court's 2018 sports betting ruling did not give states exclusive authority. He said federal regulators can oversee exchanges and states can continue regulating casinos and sportsbooks.

Meanwhile, Goldsmith Romero said the Supreme Court would likely take up the matter given the conflicting decisions across the Circuit Courts. "I think it's likely that the prediction markets may end up losing on the sports contracts," she said.

She also said the Securities and Exchange Commission could become more involved as prediction markets offer more contracts related to public companies and their stocks. She added that it would also help if both the SEC and CFTC worked together to provide more clarity.

data.title: Wheat, Corn Futures Pick Up After Selloff — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery rose 1.4% Thursday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $5.78 1/4 a bushel as grains picked up from the previous day's commodity selloff.
  • Corn for December delivery rose 0.8% to $4.39 a bushel.
  • Soybeans for January delivery fell 0.8% to $12.07 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Weak Bounce: Wheat and corn futures picked up some of the previous day's lost ground when commodities sold off broadly. Soybeans were the most resilient in the selloff and slipped a bit further Thursday.

"A range-bound trade is possible for the beans as the market monitors South American weather," Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives said in a note. "South American crop prospects look good, but there is a lot of growing season left."

Killjoy Currency: The U.S. dollar's rise to a near 20-month high is putting pressure on commodities broadly, including grains.

"The dollar has softened slightly, allowing an overnight rally, however the dollar is again showing a little strength into the mid-session which is pulling values off their highs," said Brian Hoops, president of Midwest Market Solutions.

Good early season growing conditions in South America and the stronger dollar have kept the grains in a solid downtrend, he said. "Until the technical trend changes or the dollar tops out, rallies will prove difficult to sustain."

Export Sales: Wheat sales for the 2026-27 marketing year were 344,800 metric tons in the week ended Nov. 12, up 89% from the week before, the USDA said. Soybean sales for 2026-27 rose 30% to 1.5 million tons, while corn sales fell 45% to 1.59 million tons. An additional 41,900 tons of corn were sold for the 2027-28 marketing year.

Flash Sale: The USDA reported a sale of 200,844 metric tons of soybeans for delivery to Mexico during the 2026-2027 marketing year.

INSIGHT

Going Abroad: The U.S. Agriculture Department plans trade missions to six countries in 2027, from Venezuela to South Korea, seeking improved access to global markets for U.S. producers. The 10 agribusiness trade missions held since January 2025 generated $154 million in 12-month projected sales, the USDA said.

"These results translate into better market access and increased sales for American farmers, ranchers, and producers," the USDA said. Other countries on the roster for next year are Costa Rica, Ecuador, Poland and Thailand.

On the Bright Side: U.S. corn exports are running below their year-ago levels but could get a boost, along with prices, from Europe's shortfall and Ukraine's inability to ship grains in 2026, analysts at Rabobank said in a report.

EU production was down by almost 10 million metric tons this year due to drought, and while estimates show imports up by just 2 million or 3 million tons, that could change, they said. Given damage to Ukrainian export infrastructure, "importers may be left scrambling for corn in the next year if Ukraine can't ship."

data.title: Brazil's Lula closing in on finance minister pick, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lula could name finance minister next week, sources say
  • Vice-President Geraldo Alckmin under consideration
  • Piaui Governor Rafael Fonteles also in the frame
  • Current Finance Minister Dario Durigan unlikely to stay
  • Investors are worried about economic and fiscal outlook

By Lisandra Paraguassu

Recently reelected Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is getting closer to naming his next finance minister and a decision could come next week, according to six sources familiar with the discussions.

Amid investor concern about the outlook for Brazil's economy, the top contenders are Geraldo Alckmin, currently Lula's vice president, and Rafael Fonteles, the reelected governor of Piauí state, said the sources, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity.

Reuters reported last month that Alckmin and Fonteles were frontrunners for the finance minister position, shortly after Lula secured a fourth non-consecutive term in a surprise runoff triumph.

Lula, a veteran leader of Brazil's political left, has not yet made a final decision, the sources told Reuters.

Fonteles, a trained mathematician whose fiscal policies in Piauí helped balance the state’s accounts, is viewed favorably by financial markets, one source at the president's office said.

He had dropped out of the spotlight as he focused on forming his second-term government in Piauí, but his name has gained momentum in recent days, the source said.

Alckmin also remains a strong contender.

Another presidency source said moderate public finance reforms led by Alckmin would carry more weight than ones led by anyone else, given his reputation as a fiscal conservative.

Brazilian assets have sold off sharply since Lula's reelection on October 25, in part because of worries about the outlook for public finances.

The drawback for Alckmin's candidacy is that he would be difficult to remove if needed, as Lula would struggle to dismiss his own vice president.

A Lula-allied senator said Fonteles faced a similar problem. "A newly elected governor who resigns to take on a ministerial post is also, in a sense, 'unfireable,'" the senator said.

Lula told current Finance Minister Dario Durigan that he probably will not stay in the job, the sources told Reuters.

The president has grown irritated by press speculation about his cabinet and has scolded close aides over it.

"Each ministry in this country will be appointed by me, when I want, on the day I want, and on the date I want. No one will appoint anyone through the press," he said on Thursday.

The cabinet selection puzzle also involves Lula's next chief of staff, a position that could lead to a candidacy to run for president in 2030, and leadership of the Ministry of Public Security, which Lula considers central to his final term.

Lula is set to be inaugurated on January 5, 2027, and former ministers said the full ministerial lineup may take a while. In 2022, Lula announced most of his cabinet on December 27, five days before his inauguration.

data.title: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
data.description:
President Donald Trump’s nominees to fill two vacancies at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) faced questions about investor protections, regulatory oversight and financial innovation during a Senate confirmation hearing Thursday, including scrutiny of the agency’s approach to tokenized securities.

Kristin Johnson, Trump’s Democratic nominee, backed formal rulemaking to address concerns about the agency’s exemption for tokenized stock trading.

“I feel strongly that regulation is made better through the notice and comment period,” Johnson told the Senate Banking Committee in response to Democratic Senator Angela Alsobrooks. She added that she would welcome the opportunity to address issues covered by the exemption through that process.

The SEC’s Sept. 17 exemption lets qualifying platforms trade blockchain-based versions of US-listed shares without registering as securities exchanges under certain conditions. The order took effect immediately and invites comments on possible changes.

Johnson, a former Commodity Futures Trading Commission commissioner, appeared alongside Republican Steven Levine, a former aide to SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda. If confirmed, they would bring the five-member commission to four members, with three Republicans and one Democrat.

The hearing comes as the SEC has scaled back enforcement activity and pursued regulatory changes intended to accommodate digital assets, including efforts to facilitate tokenized securities that have drawn scrutiny from lawmakers and market participants.

Companies reject tokenized stock listings

The measure has drawn objections from publicly traded companies, with 67 opposing the tokenization of their shares on the OKXICE platform, according to a Nov. 5 public notice.

Johnson also cited concerns about Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer compliance, noting that objections to the exemption extended beyond investor protection.

Levine, meanwhile, said he had not closely studied the innovation exemption but understood it to be time-limited and include investor protections. He emphasized that Congress had authorized the SEC to grant exemptions from federal securities laws when doing so serves the public interest and remains consistent with investor protection requirements.

He pointed to exchange-traded funds as an example of financial innovation that initially developed through regulatory exemptions before becoming subject to broader agency rules.

Senate weighs bipartisan SEC appointments

If confirmed, Johnson would become the SEC’s only Democratic commissioner, a development some in the crypto industry believe could strengthen the agency’s approach to regulation.

“Crypto isn’t a partisan issue, and the rules that come out of a bipartisan commission will stand on firmer footing,” Jessica Martinez, US policy director at digital asset infrastructure company Fireblocks, told Cointelegraph.

Martinez added that even minority commissioners can influence policy by challenging proposals and pushing for unresolved issues to be addressed before rules are finalized.

Senators have until noon Friday to submit additional written questions to the nominees, with responses due by 5:00 pm ET on Nov. 24, according to the committee’s closing remarks.

The nominations could then advance to a committee vote before being considered by the full Senate. Both nominees would require Senate confirmation before taking their seats at the SEC.

data.title: It’s a ‘dark period for tech’ as Anthropic debuts IPO – Dan Ives
data.description:
Anthropic's public debut marks a watershed moment for the technology sector even as broader markets endure what Dan Ives, co-partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., called "a dark period for tech" in an interview with CNBC.

While the AI company's IPO demonstrated strong institutional appetite during its roadshow, the S&P 500 (SP500) has fallen for six consecutive days, and the entire AI stock stack has pulled back sharply.

Ives described the current market environment as "a tale of two cities," with Anthropic's successful offering standing in stark contrast to widespread investor anxiety.

He attributed the tech sector's struggles to concerns surrounding Nvidia and China, as well as broader uncertainty that has sent the VIX Volatility Index to 28—its highest level since March.

Despite the turbulence, Ives characterized the downturn as "a panic moment" rather than a fundamental shift in the technology landscape.

"We're less than 15% through the build out of the AI revolution," he said, adding that the foundational bull thesis for tech remains intact.

The analyst emphasized that Anthropic's IPO could pave the way for OpenAI's expected public offering in early 2027, underscoring the continued momentum in artificial intelligence development.

He noted that if Anthropic succeeds in generating substantial annual revenue over the next five to seven years, the company could see its valuation grow significantly.

Ives pointed to expected capital expenditure growth as a key driver for the sector, projecting $1.3T to $1.5T in AI infrastructure spending next year. Anthropic , he said, will be "a huge piece of that" alongside other frontier AI models and companies in cybersecurity and software.

Looking ahead, Ives suggested that the current market anxiety will eventually be viewed as a buying opportunity.

"I think we're going to look back in this period, just like April 2025 Liberation Day, and March 2020 during COVID as the opportunity," he said, dismissing comparisons to the 2007 bubble given current valuations and growth fundamentals.

data.title: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Customer Data Leaked by Hackers — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Glickman and Alexander Saeedy

Data from thousands of customers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase was leaked Thursday by a ransomware group, the latest in a string of tech incidents that have unnerved consumers in the last week.

A Visa spokesman said no payments data, such as card numbers, were affected and Visa's own systems weren't involved or affected. It added that the incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region.

A Mastercard spokesman said the incident exposed a "limited amount of information from a subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program" He added that the exposure has been contained and that there is no impact on Mastercard's payment network or the ability of people to use their cards.

A JPMorgan spokeswoman said that third parties who provide services to the firm were targeted, and the company believes attackers accessed marketing data, potentially including customer names and email addresses. The bank said there was no disruption to its customer services.

A ransomware hacking group called n0n has claimed responsibility for the attack, according to cybersecurity firm SOCRadar.

None of the firms named the third-party company that was hacked.

The companies have millions of customers, but the hack comes as anxiety has run high about the ability of artificial-intelligence to supercharge cyberattacks and a series of tech failures spooked Americans.

Earlier this week, customers for JPMorgan Chase experienced issues accessing their accounts and sending payments, which the bank said was the result of a software update. The issue rippled across into complaints about other banks, raising fears among consumers and across the internet of widespread banking turbulence. Coupled with the Federal Aviation Administration's decision to temporarily ground all flights on Friday and an earlier disruption at Microsoft that kept people out of their emails, the country was on edge about the safety of technology critical to daily life.

"There is no connection to service disruption of some customers experienced earlier this week," JPMorgan Chase's statement said Thursday.

Write to Ben Glickman at ben.glickman@wsj.com and Alexander Saeedy at alexander.saeedy@wsj.com

data.title: Amodeis Sidestep Question on Jensen Huang — WSJ
data.description:
By Maxwell Zeff

Anthropic cofounders Dario and Daniela Amodei declined to say whether they thought former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should be reinstated during an interview with CNBC. "That's up to Nvidia," said Dario. When asked what they made of the ouster, the Amodeis cited their policy difference with Huang and work with other chip partners.

"We've been a partner to Nvidia for a long time. We work with them on data centers. We've had a long and productive partnership with them. Of course, we're not always going to agree on policy issues with our partners," Dario said.

Daniela added that Anthropic is unique in the quantity of partners it works with for compute, including Google, Broadcom and Amazon. "I do think this has been a helpful strategic advantage for us," she said of the diversity.

Anthropic has occasionally found itself at odds with Huang. Earlier this year, Dario wrote in an essay that it would be helpful for the U.S. government to help the tech industry collectively slow the development of AI models, in order to avoid antitrust concerns. Huang responded at the time by saying new laws or regulations for AI companies to properly release their products was "completely unnecessary".
